## Lessons (what this skill learned)

| # | Lesson | Root Cause | Suggested Fix | Cite | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A judge whose inputs are NARROWER than the proposer's manufactures false negatives, and a false negative looks exactly like 'the proposer is wrong'. My structural api-judge read only mouse_spot_helper.py while the candidate pool came from scanning every *.py, so it refused routes the pool had legitimately found. | judge searched a different (smaller) corpus than the proposer drew from | make the judge read the same file set the pool came from (_probe_llm_register_fill._route_files) | `_probe_llm_register_fill.py:101` | draft |
| 2 | A proof that raises before its summary line prints its failures INVISIBLY: scanning for output finds nothing, which reads as 'no problems'. A NameError in section H meant 6 stale assertions in the same file were never seen for as long as the file existed. | no summary line emitted on the exception path | wrap main in try/finally that always prints the tally, and assert every helper used is defined | `_proof_namespace_registry.py:318` | draft |
| 3 | When rules are checked in sequence, ORDER IS PART OF THE RULE. A precedence list can silently contradict the behaviour its comment describes, and the symptom is a plausible wrong class rather than an error. | The same defect appeared twice. (1) `failure_axis` documented 'lower tier wins' but numbered transient_execution as 1, so the LEAST specific class won every tie, contradicting its own docstring. (2) `_verify_link_method_c` tested `^not\s+[a-z_]+$` BEFORE the lookup rule, so `not mod_row` (a lookup miss) was read as `not module` (an absent value) and 1575 rows fell through unresolved. | Order predicates MOST SPECIFIC FIRST, and assert the precedence DIRECTLY: construct the input where two rules match and check the expected one wins. | `defect:ordering-decides-class-twice:2026-09-21` | reviewed |
| 4 | A class whose predicate requires BOTH a violation and a separate agreement cannot express a violation that is itself the finding. Taxonomy gaps are found by USING the taxonomy, not by reading it. | While classifying `member_id` (a regex match against a well-formed string) the signals `rule_key` set AND `meaning_ok` False — the most ordinary case, a rule that fired and found a violation — matched NO registered class, because _is_business also required meaning_ok. | Decide each class by the single observable that makes it citable (here: a rule_key exists), and make mutual exclusivity a CONSTRUCTION rather than an extra condition. | `failure_axis.py:120` | reviewed |
| 5 | CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS does NOT add a column to an existing table. A legacy table silently lacks the new column, and the seed dies with 'no such column'. | The live llm_model predated its DDL and lacked model_id/is_active/description. The DDL script ran without error and changed nothing. | Apply an explicit additive ALTER for every new column, and create any INDEX AFTER the ALTERs (an index inside the DDL script fails on a legacy table). | `db_schema.py:2997` | draft |
| 6 | PRAGMA foreign_keys is a NO-OP inside a transaction. A CREATE TEMP TABLE opens one, so the pragma is silently ignored and the next write dies with a FOREIGN KEY failure. | id_renumber.apply() set the pragma after creating the temp mapping table, so it never took effect. | Commit before setting the pragma, so the transaction it needs to affect has not started yet. | `id_renumber.py:216` | draft |
| 7 | A metric_target that is not a value of its metric_kind is a THRESHOLD THAT CAN NEVER BE READ. `pct` targets are 0-100; a target of 0.97 can never be reached, so the factor reports FAIL forever and the failure looks like a real defect. | `valid_phone_number_judgment` was registered with `metric_kind='pct'` and `metric_target='0.97'`. The sibling factor `phone_validity_judgment` uses `metric_target='100'` for the same kind, so the two disagree about the scale of the same unit. | Validate the target against the kind at the WRITE SITE: a `pct` target outside 0-100 is refused. Do not rely on a reader noticing, because a mis-scaled target produces a plausible number, not an error. | `_proof_factor_first_principle.py:195` | draft |

## Summary

| applicable | measured | PASS | FAIL | UNMEASURED | PROVEN |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 14 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 14 | 0 |

**UNMEASURED is not a pass.** A factor with no proof row has not been measured, and an absent measurement is not a passing one.

**PROVEN requires a STREAK, not a single proof.** A factor with one proof row is MEASURED; it becomes PROVEN only when its `proof_prefix` streak reaches the target. The streak is read from `activation_gate.streak_detail()` — the ONE definition of "streak" — so the generator and the activation gate cannot disagree about the same evidence.
